newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Police hunt serial killer of women in Estonia.
newsitem.headline: Police hunt serial killer of women in Estonia.

text.p: Estonian police have launched a manhunt for a brutal serial killer believed to be behind the murder of at least four young women in the past month.
Authorities said on Friday the killings, which have spread terror in northeastern city of Narva, were the first serial murders in the brief history of Estonia as an independent state.

Four women have been killed and a fifth is fighting for her life in hospital. All the victims, aged between 17 and 27, were brutally beaten and one was found with a noose made out of a stocking tied around her neck.
The mutilated remains of the most recent victim, an unidentified 17-year-old girl, were found on Tuesday near the Narva river.
"The monster must be caught as soon as possible," a police spokeswoman told Reuters.
Street lighting is being kept on longer than usual and authorities have appealed to factories to provide extra transport for workers on night shifts, Narva's deputy mayor Viktor Veevo said.
Textile mills working around the clock employ hundreds of women in this predominantly Russian city of 80,000.

Estonia and Baltic siblings Latvia and Lithuania have witnessed a sharp increase in violent crime since they quit the Soviet Union five years ago, and embarked on their transition to a market economy.
